full_details: At twenty to nine, from the desk under the west window, you saw the Friday litany let out. A woman came down the step with an older woman, a music-book under her arm. Dark hair under the hood, and when she looked up at the rooks, very dark eyes. She crossed toward the lane. You did not go down. She did not speak. The leaf on the desk was blank. At two you were at the Cross Keys. The part for the afternoon had no name written on it. At night, by one candle, you fair-copied a single line, with no title, no number, and no name, and you laid the leaf in the folder. You did not give it to anyone. You said four words, and no more. You put a small cross in the almanac, and no word beside it.
one_sentence: From the west window you saw a woman with very dark eyes leave the church porch, and at night you fair-copied one line and said four words.
title: A dark-eyed woman at the porch
